evidence:
Core behaviour graded: functional criteria grade the board (hro_moves, hro_bulk, hro_undo, hro_interview_places, hro_two_people incl. 409 stale move + 15 s live board), conversations (hro_messaging, hro_long_thread, hro_unread_seen) and candidate isolation (hro_candidate) in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 37-160; weights in the line-25 leg ledger (61 total).
Server-backed, not same-origin: gate hro_gate_shared (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:46-52) creates a card via UI, reloads (still signed in, card present) and reads it as the Observer in a new independent empty browser context, and explicitly rejects 'a static seed response, a no-op success message or a browser-only save'. Many scored legs re-read as Mei Lin / Aud in independent contexts (hro_moves line 42, hro_bulk line 78, hro_undo line 87, hro_activity line 96).
Restart durability (Lessons #15 pattern): hro_intake_restart (functional/judge.toml:27-34, weight 4.5, restart leg 1.5) builds several distinct revisions - two new jobs with managers/places, six ordered candidates, a move to Screen, a within-stage re-order, a rejection with suffixed reason, an internal note, a suffixed message in Noor's conversation, the unread total and J1 Activity lines, plus the seeded Platform Engineer order and Noor's seeded note - records each, calls restart_app once ('A reload is not a restart; if restart_app reports an error or cannot be called, this criterion is 0'), signs in again in a fresh independent context and requires 'everything recorded is unchanged (nothing lost, reordered or duplicated) and the starting data is not loaded again (the seeded jobs appear once)'. This is a multi-revision, real-restart, fresh-context re-read, not a single-record check. Public basis: instruction.md ('keep new work across restarts', 'Load ... once'), integration.md:8-9, hireops_rules.md:59-60 (order kept after reload, fresh sign-in or restart).
Lessons #16 (double grading): the restart leg compares against the before-restart recorded state, so a failed reject/move/message is not penalised again here; functional/prompt.md:21 makes setup legs state-relative.
Re-auth: the gate re-checks sign-in after reload; restart leg re-signs in in a fresh context; draft survival across ended session/sign-in and per-user isolation (brief + hireops_rules.md:175-182) is graded in polish hro_pol_session_resume (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:61); reload/switch survival in hro_drafts (functional line 127-133). Drafts' storage location is the builder's choice, and no criterion demands drafts survive a restart (no hidden demand).
Tooling: tests/tools/restart_mcp.py and tests/test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean); test.sh:127-193 generates the helper relaunching over the same DB_PATH as uid 65534; rewardkit runs with --max-concurrent-agent 1 (test.sh:206), so no concurrent session mutates the recorded state between record and restart; hro_intake_restart is the first functional criterion and the only one told to call restart_app (functional/prompt.md:1).
Adversarial: in-memory app passes the gate (independent context hits same process) but fails hro_intake_restart; localStorage-backed app fails the gate's independent context; reseed-on-boot app fails 'seeded jobs appear once'; app persisting cards but not notes/activity/read markers fails the recorded note/Activity/unread re-read. Conforming alternative: any storage layout, routes or labels pass; the bar only compares observed state. Limit (Note, not defect): a browser cannot prove SQLite specifically - accepted shared-runtime policy per REVIEW_POLICY 'A browser exchange cannot prove SQLite'.
Golden evidence: raw-evidence-index.json entries re-hashed - all 8 artifact hashes match and all 12 matching_source_files match the frozen task bytes. qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/workspace.cjs:557-568 kills the server (SIGTERM), relaunches over the same DB and asserts identical applications, activity, job count, per-person unread and latest message, then live updates resume; results/workspace.json: 26/26 groups passed, no page errors. This is a scripted golden check, not a configured judge run.
